key_insight: Normalizing SGD updates can accelerate learning by making the effective step size grow as gradients shrink, but this same feedback eventually causes marginal stability and changes the scaling of training time with width and batch size.
engineering_relevance: The results give practical guidance for choosing model width and batch size under a fixed compute budget, especially when using normalized or adaptive learning-rate optimizers.
method: Analyzed normalized SGD in a random-feature model with power-law teacher and data covariance.
Derived a dynamical mean-field theory for loss versus training time, model width, and batch size.
Identified late-time regimes: width-limited, edge-of-stochastic-stability, and deterministic edge-of-stability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports linearized ResNet experiments on CIFAR-5M that support the predicted acceleration, breakdown, and resource-scaling trends.
watch_item: The acceleration can disappear at finite step size as the system approaches marginal stability, so normalized updates may require careful tuning to avoid unstable training.
paper_title: A Solvable Model of Adaptive Learning Rate Rescaling: Acceleration, Stability & Scaling
